headline: Zenzap, a work chat app with built-in AI, has raised $44 million to take on WhatsApp for workplace messaging.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a mid-sized round for a young product.
importance_line: Shift workers who coordinate over personal chat apps may get a safer work option, but the company is small next to Slack and Microsoft Teams.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Zenzap, a work messaging app with built-in AI, raised $44 million from investors including Bessemer and Lightspeed, in the first fundraising for its founder Guy Weiss. The app is aimed at staff such as restaurant and retail workers who now use WhatsApp, and Weiss says those personal apps cannot support AI agents because they do not meet company IT rules.
